Class ConfigGameTests

java.lang.Object

    • serverTomlRoundTrips

      @GameTest(structure="somegoogly:empty", maxTicks=60) public void serverTomlRoundTrips(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      TomlConfig writes defaults for an absent file, then re-reads an existing file without overwriting it. In game: open a new world and serverconfig/somegoogly-server.toml appears with every key at its default; set globalPercent = 17, run /reload, and the file still says 17.

    • serverTomlReadsLiteralStringsAndRejectsWrongTypes

      @GameTest(structure="somegoogly:empty", maxTicks=60) public void serverTomlReadsLiteralStringsAndRejectsWrongTypes(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      TomlConfig reads single-quoted literal strings, keeps quoted # and ], and uses the integer default for a value of the wrong type. In game: on a Fabric server, write spawnExcludedMods = ['minecolonies', 'create'] and globalPercent = 5.0 into serverconfig/somegoogly-server.toml, run /reload, and check the log warns about globalPercent while both mods stay excluded.

    • tomlCompletionPreservesAuthoredContent

      @GameTest(structure="somegoogly:empty", maxTicks=60) public void tomlCompletionPreservesAuthoredContent(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Valid TOML syntax and table identity survive completion; malformed input is preserved. In game: quote globalPercent's key and set it to 1_0, add a comment and an unknown key, then reload. The value becomes 10 and the authored content remains. A syntax error is logged without rewriting the file.
